content:
- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in the early part of the forecast horizon (first 5–10 days).
- After a spike in price (e.g., 70s to 76s), model tends to overshoot and then gradually correct — but often lags the true decline.
- Model shows diminishing sensitivity to recent price drops; fails to adjust downward quickly when true prices fall below 70.
- Mean reversion is not captured: model holds high forecasts even when recent history shows downward momentum.
- Forecast horizon 30d is overly optimistic — true prices often settle below 73, while model stays above 72.5.
- Overshoot after spikes is common — model peaks too early and stays high longer than actual price correction.
- Model underreacts to low-price periods (e.g., 60s–65s) — fails to recognize that prices may not rebound quickly.
- True price behavior shows stronger volatility clustering — model smooths out extremes, missing sharp reversals.
